newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia intends to lower taxes, reform code by '98.
newsitem.headline: Russia intends to lower taxes, reform code by '98.

text.p: Russia intends to lower taxes and pass a reform-oriented tax code by 1998, top Russian financial officials told a conference for foreign investors on Monday.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying tax and industry reform were high priorities this year.

"My position here is clear -- next year's budget will not be considered or accepted without changes to the tax system and a decrease in the tax burden for the real sector," he told the Foreign Investment Council.
The Council groups foreign businessmen and Russian officials.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said a new tax code, developed by the Finance Ministry and under consideration by the Duma lower house of parliament, would be passed by next year.
"This is a contemporary tax code, it is practically ready, and I believe that we will live by it in 1998," he told the group.
Livshits said he did not support special tax privileges for foreign investment.
"I am not a supporter of a special regime for anyone," he said.
Businessmen say that current tax laws are contradictory and impose an unrealistic burden on companies, prompting many to evade taxes.
Russian Economy Ministry officials estimated that 1997 foreign investment would be about $6-7 billion, after $4.5 billion in the first nine months of 1996.
